plants.sentence: Assigning variants at random cannot stop anyone steering units with better prospects into one group, so that bias stays in place.
If a 95% interval for the difference does not contain 0, the two groups certainly differ, with no chance of error.
The sample needed shrinks as the effect gets smaller: halving the smallest effect you want to detect roughly halves the sample.
The Bonferroni correction divides alpha by the number of tests, so three tests at 0.05 are each judged against about 0.0167; Bonferroni first devised it for insurance mathematics.
Because results differ by browser, the browser a user chooses causes how strongly they respond to the change.
